title: South China Sea Code of Conduct: A Deal Is Not Enough
gist: As ASEAN and China aim to conclude a South China Sea Code of Conduct in 2026, the author argues the key question is whether it reduces tensions by addressing underlying drivers, not merely whether a deal is signed (truncated excerpt).

insights.claim: ASEAN and China are working to conclude a South China Sea Code of Conduct in 2026.
insights.speaker: Abdul Rahman Yaacob
insights.so_what: A signed COC is a watch item for regional maritime risk and shipping/energy exposure.

insights.claim: A deal is not enough if it does not address the underlying drivers of tension and shape actors' behavior.
insights.speaker: Abdul Rahman Yaacob
insights.so_what: Treat signing as a low-signal event; look at enforcement and behavior change.
insights.quote: A deal is not enough if it does not address the underlying drivers of tension and shape actors’ behaviors.

insights.claim: The disputes involve China and ASEAN members Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, and the COC is meant to create a rules-based framework to manage disputes, reduce miscalculation and prevent armed conflict.
insights.speaker: Abdul Rahman Yaacob
insights.so_what: Overlapping claims by five states mean any code must manage multiple bilateral frictions.
